heroHeadline: Haiti Flag Day (May 18) Eve: MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Day 8 Closed; 78+ Killed Since May 9 — Gen. Batsuuri's GSF First Week, Elections Abandoned, Artibonite Unguarded
heroSubtitle: As Haiti marks the eve of its Jour du Drapeau (Flag Day, May 18, 2026), the country faces its national holiday — celebrating the 1803 Congress of Arcahaie that produced the Haitian flag and foreshadowed independence — amid conditions Agenzia Fides characterized as 'pride and sorrow.' MSF's hospital in Cité Soleil, the only emergency medical facility for the commune's 300,000+ residents, entered its eighth consecutive day of closure on May 17, 2026, with no announced reopening timeline. UN BINUH's provisional toll from May 9–14 Cité Soleil and Croix-des-Bouquets gang clashes stands at 78 killed and 66 wounded (at least 10 confirmed civilians); the broader March 5–May 11 toll for the same zones is 305 killed and 277 wounded, including 63 confirmed civilian residents. Major General Erdenebat Batsuuri (Mongolia) begins his first full week commanding the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) with approximately 800 personnel deployed — all concentrated in Port-au-Prince's city center, with no presence in Cité Soleil, the Cul-de-Sac Plain, or the Artibonite Department. The GSF's $200M+ pledged Trust Fund remains only $59M disbursed; full 5,500-person strength is not expected until fall–end 2026. PM Fils-Aimé's May 12 declaration that August 30 elections are 'impossible' stands; no electoral decree issued; 23 communes inaccessible; 1.47M+ displaced; 5.9M face acute food insecurity; the 2026 HRP is funded at ~20% of $880M. The Washington Post investigation (May 15) documented ~$970M in US Haiti security spending since 2024 against expanding gang control. The Dominican Republic's May 2026 reopening of airspace to Cap-Haïtien remains the sole modest positive development in an otherwise deteriorating picture.
